item.title: Here is why bank transfers in Nigeria will cost more from 2026
item.description: From January 2026, sending ₦50,000 ($34.14) through your bank app could cost you ₦100 in transfer fees. Not because banks suddenly changed their pricing, but because the Nigerian government has changed who pays for electronic transfers.

item.title: How pricing, fibre and 5G collided in African telecoms in 2025
item.description: In 2025, Africa’s telecom industry entered a defining chapter. Towers and cell sites now blanket the continent, yet hundreds of millions of people still can’t afford to get online.

item.title: How DER’s Elena Dia is rethinking ecosystem building in Senegal
item.description: As Senegal’s startup ecosystem matures, DER is moving away from generic entrepreneurship support toward sector focused programmes designed to deliberately build high impact companies. In this interview, Elena Dia explains how mobile money financing, targeted acceleration, and a project driven approach are reshaping how institutions support founders across the country.

item.title: After years of financing solar, Sun King turns to smartphones in Nigeria
item.description: Sun King’s expansion into smartphone financing comes as rising smartphone prices continue to deepen Nigeria’s digital access gap.

item.title: Nomba adds Apple Pay as Nigerian businesses seek easier global payments
item.description: Nomba is the latest Nigerian fintech to integrate Apple Pay, joining Stripe-owned Paystack, which integrated Apple Pay into its payment stack for businesses in 2021, and a similar launch by cross-border payments fintech Platnova in July 2025

item.title: Nigeria’s internet penetration crosses 50%, still short of national target
item.description: Nigeria’s internet penetration crossed the 50% mark in November 2025, reaching 50.58%, according to the latest industry data from the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), signifying steady progress but well short of the 70% broadband penetration target set under the National Broadband Plan (NBP) 2020–2025, which expires in December
